chunks: He said: Ahmad ibn al-Harith narrated, elevating it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
If the Qaim arises, people would say: How can this be, when his bones have decomposed?

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim, a title for the Twelfth Imam, meaning 'The One Who Arises'
key_terms.عِظَامُهُ: His bones, referring to the physical remains of the Imam
key_terms.وَبَلَتْ: Decomposed or decayed, referring to the state of the body after death

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Qaim's bones decomposing in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) addresses the doubt of the Waqifiya regarding the death of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s). It posits that if the Qaim (Imam al-Mahdi) were to arise while people still remembered the physical death and decomposition of his father, they would question his identity due to the lingering doubt about his lineage and status.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 56 - Ahmad bin Harith has narrated directly from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:
If the Qaim arises in these circumstances, people would say: How can this person be the Qaim, when his bones have also decomposed?
